nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be computable. If a set $P$ of natural numbers is in the class $\Sigma_n$ of the arithmetical hierarchy, then so is $\{w \in \mathbb{N} : g(w) \in P\}$; and if $P$ is in the class $\Pi_n$, then so is $\{w \in \mathbb{N} : g(w) \in P\}$.
nodes.title: The hierarchy is closed under computable precomposition

nodes.summary: The pairing bijection $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, given by $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise, is a computable function of its two arguments.
nodes.title: The pairing function is computable

nodes.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. If $Q$ is a decidable set of natural numbers, then the set of pairs $(a, b) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ with $\langle a, b \rangle \in Q$ is decidable.
nodes.title: Computable predicates are closed under precomposition with pairing

nodes.summary: If $P$ is a decidable set of natural numbers and $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a computable function, then the set $\{w \in \mathbb{N} : g(w) \in P\}$ is decidable.
nodes.title: Computable predicates are closed under computable precomposition

nodes.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. The function sending $z \in \mathbb{N}$ to the first component $a$ of the unique pair $(a, b)$ with $\langle a, b \rangle = z$ is computable.
nodes.title: The first projection of the pairing function is computable

nodes.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. The function sending $z \in \mathbb{N}$ to the second component $b$ of the unique pair $(a, b)$ with $\langle a, b \rangle = z$ is computable.
nodes.title: The second projection of the pairing function is computable

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A set $P$ of natural numbers is in $\Delta_n$ when it is in both classes $\Sigma_n$ and $\Pi_n$ of the arithmetical hierarchy.
nodes.title: The class Δₙ of the arithmetical hierarchy

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, writing $\Sigma_n$ and $\Pi_n$ for the classes of the arithmetical hierarchy, every $\Sigma_n$ set of natural numbers is in $\Sigma_{n+1}$ and every $\Pi_n$ set of natural numbers is in $\Pi_{n+1}$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the hierarchy

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every set of natural numbers in the class $\Pi_n$ of the arithmetical hierarchy is also in $\Pi_{n+1}$; that is, $\Pi_n \subseteq \Pi_{n+1}$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the Π hierarchy

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every set of natural numbers in the class $\Pi_n$ of the arithmetical hierarchy is also in $\Sigma_{n+1}$; that is, $\Pi_n \subseteq \Sigma_{n+1}$, by adding a dummy existential quantifier.
nodes.title: Every Πₙ set is Σₙ₊₁

nodes.summary: Let $\Sigma_n$ and $\Pi_n$ be the levels of the arithmetical hierarchy of predicates on $\mathbb{N}$: $\Sigma_0 = \Pi_0$ is the class of computable predicates, $P \in \Sigma_{n+1}$ when for some $Q \in \Pi_n$ and all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for some $y$, and $P \in \Pi_{n+1}$ when for some $Q \in \Sigma_n$ and all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for all $y$; here…
nodes.title: Every Σₙ predicate is Σₙ₊₁

nodes.summary: A predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$ is recursively enumerable if and only if it is in $\Sigma_1$, that is, if and only if there is a computable predicate $Q$ on $\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for some $y$, where $\langle x, y \rangle$ is the standard pairing function of $\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Σ₁ is the class of recursively enumerable predicates

nodes.summary: Let $\Sigma_n$ and $\Pi_n$ be the levels of the arithmetical hierarchy of predicates on $\mathbb{N}$: $\Sigma_0 = \Pi_0$ is the class of computable predicates, $P \in \Sigma_{n+1}$ when for some $Q \in \Pi_n$ and all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for some $y$, and $P \in \Pi_{n+1}$ when for some $Q \in \Sigma_n$ and all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for all $y$; here…
nodes.title: Σₙ and Πₙ predicates are Δₙ₊₁

nodes.summary: Let $\Sigma_n$ and $\Pi_n$ be the levels of the arithmetical hierarchy of predicates on $\mathbb{N}$: $\Sigma_0 = \Pi_0$ is the class of computable predicates, $P \in \Sigma_{n+1}$ when for some $Q \in \Pi_n$ and all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for some $y$, and $P \in \Pi_{n+1}$ when for some $Q \in \Sigma_n$ and all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for all $y$; here…
nodes.title: Every Σₙ predicate is Πₙ₊₁

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
